Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

please leave the preview in a review state while we check it and note which fields the two staff members are meant to inspect the request is to arrange the existing sample and its images for comparison not to finish the catalog the collection covers ferry office material from 1986 through 2004 the sample has seven records and the first batch has 240 paper items with 32 scans so those counts should remain clear anywhere they are repeated after the assistant and volunteer have reviewed the layout we can record their questions in the internal notes the uncertain east slip or east ship title should remain uncertain until someone checks the sheet the access sentence should remain a draft and the public link should stay conditional on the access review rather than on the festival date", "output": "We are setting up an archive preview for the fictional Bellwether Harbor records room, and I want the first pass to stay on the local review computer rather than the public site. The collection covers ferry office material from 1986 through 2004, and the preview is for two staff members to check descriptions before anyone discusses release. The archive has 18 cartons in the storage list, and 6 of those cartons contain tide schedules, so please keep the carton count and the schedule count separate. The room has a long worktable with space for three open boxes and a small scanner beside the monitor. I am not asking for a new catalog or a public launch. I need a working preview that lets us inspect what is already described.

We have about 240 paper items in the first batch, but only 32 have been scanned so far. The scanner is set to 120 dpi for the reading copies, and the preservation files are handled elsewhere. Do not imply that all 240 items are online. The 32 scans include handwritten shift sheets, printed notices, and two folded route maps. The maps are each stored as one record, even though each map has a front and a back. The date range on the folder is 1986 to 2004, but several notices have no exact day written on them. A blank day should remain blank rather than being filled from a nearby schedule. The staff want to compare the item description with the image without losing their place in the list.

On the preview screen, there should be four tabs called Records, Images, Notes, and Access. The Records tab is the starting view, and it should show seven test records before the full batch is added. The seven are not a count of everything in the archive, just the sample we will use in the room. Each row needs a short title, a date field, and a source carton field. Put the source carton field after the date field because people keep scanning across the screen for it. The Images tab can show the 32 scans and should not claim that the remaining items have image files. The Notes tab is only for internal checking, and the Access tab can show the current access wording without treating it as an approval.

First, show the title and date in the record row. Second, put the carton reference after the date. Third, keep the image preview beside the description on a wide monitor and below the description on a narrow one. The narrow display is 11 inches across, and the wide monitor is 24 inches across. Those are screen widths, not image sizes. Do not change the scan resolution to make the images fit. The preview can scale a copy on screen while keeping the stored file untouched. For these checks, keep the label visible beside each image and in the list. The configuration key is
preview.show_labels
We need that literal key in the setup notes because the technician will search for it directly, and the label behavior should not be described as a new record field.

There are two staff members checking the screen. One is a collections assistant, and one is the ferry office volunteer who knows the old route names. The assistant will check spelling and carton references, while the volunteer will check whether the titles match the handwriting. Do not make the volunteer responsible for access decisions. If a title is uncertain, keep the uncertainty in a note rather than guessing. One penciled sheet looks like it says “east slip,” but it could say “east ship,” and the volunteer has not checked that sheet yet. Another record has the clear title “night crossing roster,” and the date field says November 1998 with no day. I heard the assistant say, “We can leave that one as November for now,” which is a reminder not to manufacture a day.

For the internal note field, use plain text and let staff enter a question without changing the public description. For example, the assistant might write, “Is this the launch notice from the north pier, or is it the later copy from the ticket desk?” That is a question, not a claim. The note can also mention an unreadable stamp or a mismatch between the folder and a sheet. Please keep names of people out of the preview sample because the first batch includes two envelopes with personal correspondence. They are counted among the 240 paper items, but they are not part of the 32 scans in this preview. The archive lead has not decided whether those envelopes can be described at item level, so the sample should not resolve that question.

For access wording, we have a draft sentence that says, “Reading copies are available for staff review,” and that wording is still under discussion. The word “staff” matters because we do not have permission to say that the files are open to visitors. A person asked whether the public view could be switched on for the harbor festival in June, and I said that depends on the access review being completed first. If the review is not complete, the preview must remain on the local review computer, even if someone asks for a public link. This condition needs to be visible in the setup request because the festival date is not a release date. The date of the festival is June 14, and the review meeting is penciled in for June 6, but neither date changes the access wording by itself.

We are using the TideBoard catalog interface on the review computer, and it has one shared sign-in for the room. The interface remembers the last selected tab, but it should open on Records when a new preview session begins. The screen should not display a total for the 240 items next to the seven sample records because those numbers refer to different sets. A small note above the list can say “sample records,” and the Images tab can say “32 scanned items.” The two route maps should remain recognizable as two records with separate front and back views rather than four records. The source carton references are B03 through B20, and the six schedule cartons are B03, B05, B08, B11, B16, and B19. Those identifiers are storage references and should not be converted into dates.

When we test the layout, ask the assistant to open a record with an image and then a record without an image. The second record should still show its title, date, and carton reference without an empty picture box taking up half the row. If a record has no exact day, the date display should not add the first day of the month as a substitute. When the narrow screen stacks the image below the description, the title should remain above both parts. The volunteer said, “It is easier to read the handwriting when the image is large enough,” but that was about viewing on screen and not a request to alter the stored scans. The setup can include a preview scale control if one already exists in TideBoard, but do not make a new editing tool part of this request.

Please leave the preview in a review state while we check it, and note which fields the two staff members are meant to inspect. The request is to arrange the existing sample and its images for comparison, not to finish the catalog. The collection covers ferry office material from 1986 through 2004. The sample has seven records, and the first batch has 240 paper items with 32 scans, so those counts should remain clear anywhere they are repeated. After the assistant and volunteer have reviewed the layout, we can record their questions in the internal notes. The uncertain “east slip” or “east ship” title should remain uncertain until someone checks the sheet. The access sentence should remain a draft, and the public link should stay conditional on the access review rather than on the festival date."}]
